Someone Bought a New Porsche 911 for $151,800, 2,500 Miles Later, They Put It Up for Sale
14 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Can we interest you in an almost-new Porsche 911 Carrera T Coupe with one owner in the papers? If you said yes, then you have come to the right place, as this one is up for grabs.
It is a 2026 model year sports car that the seller bought new in September 2025, paying $151,800, as per the attached window sticker. After putting some 2,500 miles (~4,000 km) on it since, they decided to let it go, without revealing why. The car is located in Ontario, California, has a clean title, has never been involved in an accident, and has no mileage discrepancies.
There is no known flaws category in the ad, which we will link toward the end of this story, and that’s not exactly a surprise, is it? After all, we are talking about a still-new product, albeit one that shows a tiny bit of wear on the driver’s seat outer bolster, as you can see in the photo gallery above. This Porsche 911 had its 10,000-mile (~16,000 km) service performed a couple of months ago, in September 2026, at 2,228 miles (3,586 km), and has had its engine oil and filter changed.
Photo: Cars&Bids As a result, all it needs is some gasoline in the tank, and a new owner to enjoy it on a daily basis. The vehicle features 20-inch front and 21-inch rear wheels, a power-operated sunroof, leather and Sport-Tex upholstery, heated front seats with power adjustment, a Bose premium sound system, a surround view camera system, and an extended-range fuel tank. It is presented in Vanadium Gray Metallic, and other than the dashcam, it has zero modifications.
Power is supplied by a flat-six (d’oh) engine with twin-turbocharging, and a 3.0-liter displacement. It produces 388 hp (343 ps/252 kW ) and 332 lb-ft (450 Nm) of torque, with everything channeled to the rear wheels through a six-speed manual transmission. The 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) takes a little over 4 seconds, and on summer tires, the Porsche 911 Carrera T Coupe hits up to 183 mph (295 kph).
This 992 is accompanied by the owner’s manuals, the window sticker, some service records, and two keys. It’s worth noting that there is a loan on this car, and the sale proceeds will be used to satisfy it, as only then the title will become available. Interested parties should also know that full PPF has been applied to the vehicle’s exterior. The windshield sits under a clear protection film, and the windows have been ceramic tinted.
The Porsche 911 in question is advertised on Cars&Bids, with a high bid of $100,911 at the time of writing, and six days left in the ongoing online auction. The gavel will hit the table on December 3, 2026, and if you want it, then you can bid on it here .
